summary: The original Brass, set in Lancashire's cotton industry, plays much like Birmingham but with a tighter, more linear network and slightly less variability. It's a classic heavy economic game about timing your industry development against a fluctuating market.
praised: Tight, elegant economic design that rewards planning
Strong sense of building an industrial-era empire
criticised: Steep learning curve and unforgiving mistakes
Feels more austere and less varied than Birmingham's later redesign
Low direct interaction can feel isolating

interaction.detail: As in its successor, industries and rail/canal links are built onto a single shared map, and coal, iron and beer come from common markets that empty out with use, letting players box each other out of routes or cheap resources. Interaction stays indirect, through shared space and shared markets rather than direct attacks.

subsystems: network & industry development engine (build links and industry tiles, then flip/use them for VP)
sources: canal links (VP per gold circle in connected locations)
rail links (VP per gold circle in connected locations)
industry tiles by type (cotton mills, coal mines, iron works, breweries, ports) scored on flipping
leftover money converted to VP (1 VP per £10) at game end
scoring.how_you_win: Across the Canal Era and Rail Era, each of which ends when the draw deck and all hands are exhausted, players build and flip industry tiles and connect them with canals/rail; VP are tallied at the end of each era from flipped tiles, links, and leftover cash, and the highest total after both eras wins.
